q: 1. Why perspective drawing is done by manufacturer?
options: It is easy to express in the market
explain: Its primary benefit for manufacturers is that it presents the product in a visually appealing, realistic manner.

q: 2. A point is 20 mm below HP and 30 mm behind VP. Its top view will be .............
explain: The top view of a point shows its distance behind VP; since the point is below HP, its top view is conventionally drawn above the XY line, at a distance equal to the distance behind VP, i.e., 30 mm above XY.

q: 3. In orthographic projection which one have all three views same
explain: A cube looks like a square from all principal sides, and a sphere looks like a circle from every direction.

q: 4. If both the front and the top views of a point lie on the same side of the reference line the point may be situated in following angels .............
explain: When both views fall on the same side of the XY line, the point lies in either the second angle (above HP, behind VP) or the fourth angle (below HP, in front of VP), both of which yield views on the same side of the reference line.

q: 5. Which is not pictorial projection?
explain: Pictorial projections (Isometric, Oblique, Perspective) show 3D views; trigonometric is a mathematical field, not a projection type.

q: 6. If top view of a point is situated 60 mm below the reference line and its front view is 20 mm above the top view, the point lies in .............
explain: A top view below XY indicates the point is in front of VP; a front view further below (only 20mm above the very low top view, i.e., also below XY) indicates it is below HP too — this combination (in front of VP, below HP) places the point in the fourth angle.

q: 7. View of circle in orthographic is
explain: A circle appears as a circle if parallel to the plane, but as an ellipse or a line if inclined to the plane.

q: 8. If a line if parallel to both HP and VP, it true length will be seen in .............
explain: A line parallel to both principal planes is not foreshortened in either projection, so its true length appears in both the front view and the top view simultaneously.

q: 9. In orthographic projection, projector lines are
explain: Projectors in orthographic projection are parallel to each other and perpendicular (vertical) to the plane of projection.

q: 10. If the apparent and the true inclinations of a line with HP are equal, the line is .............
explain: The apparent and true inclinations of a line with HP coincide only when the line is parallel to VP, since there is then no distortion of the angle in the front view.

q: 11. In third angle projection top view is put
explain: In Third Angle Projection, the observer 'looks through' the plane, so the Top View is placed above the Front View.

q: 12. The point at which the line intersects the VP, extended if necessary, is known as .............
explain: The point where a line (extended if necessary) meets the Vertical Plane is called the Vertical Trace (VT) of the line.

q: 13. In first angle projection, the object comes
explain: In first angle projection the object is placed in the first quadrant, between the observer and the plane of projection.

q: 14. In case of third angle projection, plan is kept at
explain: Note: Plan (Top View) is above Front View, but some contexts refer to the position relative to the ground line. Based on standard key: 'below'.

q: 15. In isometric projection, dimension lines are drawn
explain: To remain consistent with the pictorial form, isometric dimension lines are drawn parallel to the isometric axes.

q: 16. In case of orthographic projection the number of view generally used are .............
explain: Although a fully described solid could theoretically use up to six principal views, in general engineering practice, orthographic projection typically uses four views (or fewer) — commonly front, top, and one or two side views — to adequately describe an object.

q: 17. Isometric projection of a sphere is a circle having a diameter
explain: Because a sphere looks the same from every direction, its isometric projection is a true circle equal to the sphere's actual diameter.

q: 18. The other name of axonometric projection is
explain: Axonometric projection represents 3D objects on a single (one) plane of projection.

q: 19. As the distance of an object from the observer increases, its size in the perspective view .............
explain: In perspective projection, objects farther from the observer subtend a smaller visual angle, so their apparent size in the perspective view decreases with increasing distance, matching real-world visual perception.

q: 20. The imaginary vertical plane passing through the observer's eye is called .............
explain: The central plane is the imaginary vertical plane passing through the observer's eye (station point) and perpendicular to the picture plane, used as a reference in perspective construction.

q: 21. In isometric projection, circles are represented as ellipse on
explain: Since all three isometric faces are inclined to the line of sight, circles on any face appear as ellipses.

q: 22. Axonometric view/drawing is what type of view?
explain: It belongs to the category of single-plane pictorial projections.

q: 23. The imaginary horizontal plane passing through the observer's eye is called .............
explain: The horizon plane is the imaginary horizontal plane that passes through the observer's eye level; its intersection with the picture plane gives the horizon line, on which vanishing points lie.

q: 24. Axonometric drawing is a drawing like
explain: In axonometric projection, the projectors are perpendicular (orthogonal) to the plane of projection.

q: 25. In one plane drawing, which one does not falls under
explain: Standard orthographic projection usually involves multiple planes (multi-view); axonometric, oblique, and dimetric are single-plane pictorials.

q: 26. A 100 m long line making 30 degree with the vertical, show its projection on horizontal plane
explain: Projection on HP = $L \times \sin(\theta)$ if angle is with vertical. $100 \times \sin(30^{\circ}) = 100 \times 0.5 = 50\text{ m}$.

q: 27. Axonometric projection is a special types of
explain: Axonometric is a sub-type of orthographic projection because the projectors are perpendicular to the plane.

q: 28. In case of dimetric projection
options: two sides are not equally inclined
explain: In Dimetric projection, two of the three axes are equally inclined to the plane of projection.

q: 29. When the picture plane coincides with the object, the perspective of the object will be of its
explain: If the picture plane passes through the object itself, there is no projection scaling, so the perspective is the same size as the object.

q: 30. If the front view of a line is parallel to the xy line its true length is shown in .............
explain: If the front view of a line is parallel to XY, the line is parallel to the profile plane, and its true length is revealed in the side (profile) view.

q: 31. If a thin set-square is kept perpendicular to both the horizontal and vertical planes, its true shape is seen in .............
explain: A plane perpendicular to both HP and VP is, by definition, parallel to the profile plane (PP), so its true shape appears in the side (profile) view.

q: 32. The perspective of a circle. When its plane is parallel to other picture plane, is .............
explain: When a circle's plane is parallel to the picture plane, there is no distortion due to angle, so its perspective projection remains a circle (though possibly scaled).

q: 33. The plane on which perspective is formed is called
explain: The perspective image of an object is projected onto the vertical picture plane.

q: 34. The view actually appears to the observer when viewed from a fixed position is called:
explain: A perspective view replicates how an object actually appears to the eye from a fixed viewing point, including apparent size reduction with distance.

q: 35. Planes which are inclined to both the horizontal and vertical planes are called .............
explain: A plane inclined to both HP and VP simultaneously (not perpendicular to either) is termed an oblique plane.

q: 36. An isometric projection is pictorial drawing of
explain: Isometric projection is a pictorial representation that shows three faces (views) of an object in a single drawing.

q: 37. A right circular cone when cut by a plane parallel to its generator, the curve obtained is a .............
explain: When a cutting plane is parallel to one generator (slant side) of a right circular cone, the section produced is a parabola, per the standard classification of conic sections.

q: 38. Name the curve traced out by a point on the circumference of a circle, which rolls outside another circle of same diameter .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, this is marked as hypocycloid; conventionally a circle rolling outside another circle of equal diameter traces a cardioid, but the given answer key selects the hypocycloid option.

q: 39. Axonometric projection is
explain: Axonometric projection is a category of orthographic (parallel) projection where the object is rotated to show multiple faces.

q: 40. The isometric length of the edge of the cube is obtained by .............
explain: Note: per the answer key this option is marked correct; conventionally the isometric length is obtained by multiplying the true length by the isometric ratio (~0.816), which corresponds to option (c) rather than 'adding.'

q: 41. When a circle rolls inside another circle of twice its diameter, the curve traced out by a point on the circumference of the rolling circle will be .............
explain: A special case of the hypocycloid: when a rolling circle's diameter is exactly half that of the fixed circle, the traced curve degenerates into a straight line (a diameter of the fixed circle) — known as the Tusi couple.

q: 42. The section obtained when the section plane is inclined to the axis of cone and cuts all the generators on either side of the apex, is called ...........
explain: When the cutting plane is inclined to the axis and cuts all generators, the resulting conic section is an ellipse.

q: 43. The section obtained when the section plane is inclined to the axis of cone, but parallel to one of the generators of a cone is called .............
explain: A plane parallel to a single generator (or 'slant edge') of a cone produces a parabola.

q: 44. The isometric view of sphere is .............
explain: Since a sphere is symmetric in every direction, its isometric projection (drawn to true/isometric scale) appears simply as a circle.

q: 45. The section obtained when the section plane makes a smaller angle with its axis than that of the angle made by the generator of a cone is called .............
explain: If the plane's angle with the axis is smaller than the generator's angle (making it 'steeper'), a hyperbola is formed.

q: 46. Name the curve traced out by a point on the circumference of a circle, which rolls on another circle of larger diameter .............
explain: Note: per the answer key this is marked 'none of these'; conventionally, a circle rolling on the outside of a larger fixed circle traces an epicycloid, but the given key selects 'none of these' for this item.

q: 47. The section obtained when the section plane passes parallel to the base of a cone is called .............
explain: A horizontal cut (parallel to the base) through a right circular cone always results in a circle.

q: 48. The section obtained when the section plane passes through the apex of the cone in such a way that it is perpendicular to the base is called.....
explain: A vertical cut passing through the apex of a cone reveals its triangular cross-section.

q: 49. First angle projection method and third angle projection method are used in .............
explain: First-angle and third-angle are the two internationally recognized conventions specifically for orthographic (multiview) projection, differing in the relative position of the object, plane, and observer.

q: 50. The receding lines in an isometric projection are drawn
explain: The receding lines in an isometric drawing that represent depth are drawn parallel to the corresponding isometric axis.
